description: Add one person by email address. An address already here, in any letter case, answers 409 with `details.contactId`. To add or fill in many at once, use upsert_contacts. The address is checked first: a refused one answers 400 with `params.issue` naming why (missing_at, display_name, domain_invalid…). The address is also checked when you hold the validate permission and address checks are turned on (get_email_check_setup): `checking` in the answer shows that check, and `checkAddresses: false` skips it. Checks never refuse the write: when this month's address checks are used up, the workspace's last payment didn't go through, or our team suspended the workspace, the contacts are saved and their checks wait on hold until the 1st of next month or the plan has room (`workspace_limit`), until the payment goes through (`payment_failed`), or until the suspension is lifted (`workspace_suspended`).

checkAddresses.description: Check the new contact's address. The answer's `checking` shows the check that started. True by default. It needs the validate permission and address checks turned on (get_email_check_setup). Without either, nothing is checked. If this month's address checks are used up, what you sent is still saved. The checks wait on hold until the 1st of next month or until the plan has room.

idempotencyKey.description: Your own id for this one call, such as a UUID, up to 255 characters. If the call fails with no answer, call again with the same key and the same arguments: within 24 hours, a saved answer comes back instead of a second run. A call left unanswered can run again after 15 minutes, so a send also keeps its intentKey or draft revision.
